country: # --- Kent / Sussex / Hampshire / Isle of Wight

name: Camber Sands
notes: Launch only in the year-round kite zone at the eastern (Jury's Gap / Broomhill) end. Best 3 h either side of low tide; groynes and shore break near high water. Alternative: Greatstone (Littlestone), 8 km E, works in N–NE.

name: Seasalter (Whitstable)
notes: Shallow estuary flats; mid to high tide, long walk at low water.

name: Shoebury East Beach
notes: Designated kite area; shallow lagoons between sandbanks at low tide, flat water, beginner friendly.

name: Felixstowe Ferry
notes: Deben river mouth: mirror-flat lagoon on the ebb and at low tide; avoid the flood (current sets into the river).

name: Sea Palling
notes: Artificial offshore reefs: flat lagoons inside, punchy waves outside; strong rips at the reef gaps.

name: Hunstanton
notes: Flat shallow water over the sandbar at low tide; do not launch between the groynes. Rare west-facing east-coast beach. Alternative: Brancaster (12 km E, NT kite zone, strong tides, experienced only).

name: Cleethorpes (Humberston)
notes: Kites zoned south of the leisure centre (Thorpe Park / Humberston Fitties end). Lagoon around mid tide, beginner friendly.

name: Redcar – Majuba
notes: Main Teesside spot, WNW through N to E. Rock reefs to the east uncover at low tide. Alternative: Seaton Carew across the Tees, flattish in southerlies.

name: Blyth – Seaton Sluice
notes: Kiters use the Seaton Sluice (south) end of the bay. Groynes and shore dump at high tide. Alternative: Tynemouth Longsands (busy surf beach).

name: Beadnell Bay
notes: Reef break plus lagoon, best mid to high tide; local BKSA school. Alternative: Budle Bay tidal lagoon around high water (1 Apr–31 Oct only).

name: West Kirby
notes: Dee estuary: kite only around high tide (no kitesurfing within 100 m of the tide line otherwise). Alternatives: Hoylake – Red Rocks (mid to high tide), Wallasey / New Brighton (NW, low tide lagoon).

name: St Annes
notes: Club spot by the Beachcomber café. Launch ~2 h before high tide; no beach on big springs, long walk at low.

name: Walney Island – Earnse Bay
notes: Gently shelving, exposed to the Irish Sea; kite school on the beach.

name: Brean
notes: Huge tidal range: very long walk over sand and mud at low water. Alternative: Weston-super-Mare – Uphill kite zone (±3 h around high tide).

name: Saunton Sands
notes: Kite zone starts past the White Rock marker ~400 m down the beach. No kitesurfing in July and August. Alternative: Westward Ho! (sand-sports zone in summer, low tide).

name: Watergate Bay
notes: Marked Kitesports Zone north of the rocks. No kiting 2 h either side of high tide; keep out of the lifeguard flags in season. Alternative: Perran Sands (north end only).

name: Gwithian
notes: St Ives Bay. Kites off limits 10:00–18:00 from mid-July to early September and between the lifeguard flags.

name: Marazion – Long Rock
notes: Mount's Bay, beginner friendly in the prevailing SW (cross-on).

name: Bantham
notes: Avon estuary mouth opposite Bigbury. Low tide to 1–2 h before high; stay right of the RNLI flags, 50 m from swimmers/surfers.

name: Exmouth
notes: Duck Pond: flat estuary lagoon, launch from the Imperial Recreation Ground; stay west of the yellow buoys 15 Sept–31 Dec (Brent geese). Seafront: ±2 h around high tide.

name: Weymouth – Portland Harbour
notes: Flat water in most winds, any tide. Launch Ferrybridge / Hamm Beach; Portland Port permit and third-party insurance required. Fast ebb through Ferrybridge. Alternative: Overcombe in Weymouth Bay (bump and jump, waves in easterlies).

name: Poole Harbour – Shore Road
notes: Whitley Lake, Sandbanks: flat shallow harbour water; Poole Harbour Commissioners kite permit required. Best mid to high tide; boat traffic. Alternative in easterlies: Studland – Knoll Beach NT kite zone (permit).

name: Ryde – Appley
notes: Solent shore: shallow sandbars and pools at low tide, waist deep at half tide.

name: Hayling Island
notes: Official kite beach just east of the Beachlands funfair (free, no safety cover); CBK club at the west end. Keep 2 line lengths off the shore in swim season. Alternative: West Wittering (2XS members only).

name: Lancing
notes: Designated kitesports zone (beginner and advanced sections); stay out of the swim zones 1 May–30 Sept. Best 3–4 h either side of high tide.

name: Kinmel Bay
notes: Flat water in WSW through N to NE. Council kite permit required (day or annual).

name: Rhosneigr
notes: Anglesey's main spot (Traeth Llydan / Crigyll): waves and big air. Rips near the river and the south end, yellow-buoyed lanes.

name: Black Rock Sands
notes: Kitesurfing allowed all year (land kiting banned Mar–Nov). Flat in light winds, small waves in strong ones.

name: Borth – Ynyslas
notes: Dyfi estuary mouth: kite at high tide; strong tidal currents, no swimming.

name: Newgale
notes: Pembrokeshire's most popular kite beach, school on site. No launching at high tide. Alternative: Freshwater West (big surf, reef, experienced only).

name: Rest Bay (Porthcawl)
notes: Any tide; Atlantic swell.

name: Longniddry Bents
notes: Edinburgh's main kite beach; best around low tide.

name: Balmedie
notes: Flat lagoons at low tide; rip strongest at mid tide, submerged posts at high tide. Alternative: Newburgh – Ythan estuary flat water 2–3 h around high tide.

name: Fraserburgh
notes: Large bay, best on the incoming tide; waves in W wind with NW swell.

name: Lossiemouth – East Beach
notes: Alternative: Findhorn (flat bay inside around high tide).

name: Machrihanish
notes: Kintyre's big Atlantic beach: launch near the village in SW, at Westport in S–SE. Shore break in W–NW.

name: Troon – South Beach
notes: Alternative: Barassie, Troon's north bay: long, wide and flat, popular teaching spot.

name: Tiree – Gott Bay
notes: Long shallow bay: beginner, freestyle and freeride; flat water in SW. Other Tiree spots: Balephetrish (N, reef-protected flat water), Crossapol (S, large easy beach).

name: Tiree – The Maze
notes: Open to all Atlantic swell; Tiree Wave Classic venue. Other Tiree wave spots: Balevullin (NW, best waves, limited space), Balephuil (SW, down-the-line in W).

name: Portstewart Strand
notes: 3 km beach break, best W–SW with small swell; strong rips. Alternative: Benone Strand (N-facing, 10 km W).

name: Strangford Lough – Newtownards
notes: Kite community at Newtownards Sailing Club; good in southerlies, patchy in northerlies. Keep clear of birds (overwintering Oct–Mar, Brent geese from late Aug).

name: Tyrella
notes: Dundrum Bay: small kickers to medium waves, onshore beginner friendly in S.
